docs/CHANGELOG.md:74:- **AWS account onboarding: welcome mail, direct and guided risk assessments** — the "new AWS account discovered → mail the owner and start an assessment" path becomes a three-mode capability, and the scoping decision moves to the person who actually knows. `WELCOME_ONLY` sends a welcome mail from a classpath template; `DIRECT` additionally starts an assessment for a use case the operator names (today's behaviour); `GUIDED` mails the owner a **one-time, expiring link** whose answers resolve through admin-configured rules into a *set* of use cases, and creates the assessment only on submit, scoped to the **union** of every matching rule. All three run from CLI (`--onboarding-mode`, `--welcome-email`, `--questionnaire-expiry-days` on `import` and `import-s3`), REST and MCP, all dry-runnable, plus a first-class `simulate-onboarding` verb (CLI + REST + MCP `simulate_account_onboarding`) that runs the whole path against a made-up account id and address — the *same* code path a real import runs, not a mock, which is what makes it a rehearsal and why it is rate limited, audited, and stamps every simulated mail with "this is a test, sent by <actor>". **The backward-compatibility contract is the load-bearing part**: a caller sending only `startRiskAssessment=true` — every `extensions/` client, `import-s3`, both existing E2E drivers — resolves to `DIRECT` **with no welcome mail**, byte-identical to before, reconciled in one function (`AccountOnboardingMode.resolve`); an explicit non-`DIRECT` mode combined with that flag is rejected, never guessed. **The matcher never decides**: it sees only choice ids (a BOOLEAN question is two choices, no second code path), every matching active rule contributes and nothing wins, `priorityOrder` is display order only, the single `isDefault` rule is consulted **after** everything else fails, and a resolution producing no requirements in the ACTIVE release is an error rather than an empty questionnaire. Answers that match nothing are **persisted** and the invite stays usable, so an admin can add the missing rule and the owner's original link still works. Rules are normalized tables, not a `ruleJson` blob (`DemandClassificationRule`'s precedent exists for a recursive condition; this one is a flat AND over choice ids, and the rule→use-case link needs real FK integrity). **The public questionnaire is the first genuinely unauthenticated write path in the codebase** and is treated as such: 256-bit `SecureRandom` token (not `UUID.randomUUID()`, because this token *creates* an assessment), single use enforced by a guarded UPDATE **claimed before** creation, 14-day expiry, a byte-identical 404 for malformed/unknown/expired/used/cancelled so the endpoint is no enumeration oracle, the account id **masked** to four digits and the owner email never returned, a new bounded fixed-window rate limiter with a dedicated failed-lookup bucket, `@Secured(IS_ANONYMOUS)` explicit on every method plus an `intercept-url-map` entry so a stale `secman_auth` cookie cannot 401 an owner out of their own link, and the full token never logged, never returned by any API, never printed by the CLI, never in an MCP result and never minted by a dry run — all asserted. Unanswered invites get one reminder then lapse; **nothing is ever auto-created**, because an assessment scoped by a guess looks authoritative and is not. `createAssessment` now takes `useCases: Set<UseCase>` (`use_case_name` widened 255→1024 in V253) and `sendStartNotification` was promoted to `notifyAssessmentStarted` so the guided path reuses the identical mail. Five private helpers were extracted from `AwsAccountRiskAssessmentService` into `EmailTemplateRenderer` — with a **closed template allowlist**, because the basenames are operator config and interpolating one into `getResourceAsStream` would be a classpath-traversal read — and the twice-copied recipient regex into `EmailAddressValidator`. New: ADMIN-**or-SECCHAMPION** admin API and UI (a deliberate widening vs Demand Classification's read-both/write-ADMIN, with a coverage matrix that shows which answer combinations would dead-end *before* an owner hits one), `/onboarding/[token]` public page, `docs/ACCOUNT_ONBOARDING.md` with 28 worked examples covering every mode × dry-run × surface, and the `/account-onboarding` skill in both trees. **OWASP: A01/A02/A03/A04/A05/A07/A08/A09 touched — 0 BLOCK.** **The Kotlin and CLI halves are compile-unverified**: the session had Java 21 only, no Gradle 9.7.0 distribution (services.gradle.org 403s through the agent proxy) and no Maven Central route. The frontend is fully verified — `npm ci`, `npm run build` and 149 unit tests green — as are the skill-sync gate and the driver's bash syntax.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:79:- **AWS account risk assessment: validation pass, three defects closed** — a review of the opt-in auto-start path (`manage-user-mappings import --start-risk-assessment --risk-usecase <name>`, mirrored on `import-s3`, REST `POST /api/user-mappings/bulk` and MCP `import_user_mappings`) confirmed the contract holds — the flag is off by default, the use case comes from a flag, and without the flag the import runs exactly as before — and turned up three things that did not. **(1) The deadline had no upper bound.** `validateStartRequest` rejected `< 1` and nothing else, so `--risk-deadline-days 2147483647` produced an `endDate` outside the SQL `DATE` range; because assessments are started *after* the mapping import commits, that surfaced as a per-account error with the mappings already persisted, and a merely absurd value like `100000` (one keystroke from `1000`) was accepted silently into an assessment the reminder scheduler — which looks two days ahead — would never wake up for. Now `MAX_DEADLINE_DAYS = 3650`, checked in `validateStartRequest` so REST and MCP share it, mirrored as `UserMappingCliService.MAX_RISK_DEADLINE_DAYS` in both CLI commands (the CLI is a separate Gradle module and cannot reference the backend constant; `ImportCommandTest` pins the two together), and clamped rather than thrown in `startAssessmentsForNewAccounts` for a direct service call, since that runs past the commit point. The MCP input schema now advertises `maximum`. **(2) The idempotent skip was reported as a failure.** When a pair already had an open assessment, `createAssessment` returned "an open risk assessment (id=…) already exists" in `AccountRiskAssessmentInfo.error`, so both CLI commands printed it as ❌/FAILED, counted it in `riskAssessmentFailures` and exited 1 — for an outcome that is the feature working correctly. The DTO gained `skipped` / `skipReason` (and the MCP result the same two fields), `error` stays null, and both CLIs render it as a skip that does not affect the exit code. **Load-bearing detail:** the owner-notification gate used to rely on `error != null` to suppress the duplicate mail, so it now tests `!info.skipped` as well — otherwise every re-import would re-notify. The path is only reachable when the mapping row was deleted and the account is imported again while its assessment is still open; a plain re-import never reaches the guard, because the account is no longer new. **(3) The email boundary was too loose.** `UserMappingService.emailRegex` was `^[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+$`, and `[^@]` matches control characters, spaces and commas — so `alice\r\nBcc: x@evil.com` passed validation. That address is not just a row: it becomes the SMTP recipient of the start and reminder mails, it is interpolated into log lines (`Started risk assessment … owner={}`), and it is written into the assessment's `notes`. The pattern now excludes whitespace and `, ; : < > " \` (a comma makes `InternetAddress.parse` split one recipient into two; a CR/LF reaches a log line), length is capped at the 255-char column width so an overlong address fails as one ordinary row error instead of a post-commit `DataException`, and the three "invalid …" messages that echo the rejected value run it through `sanitizeForMessage` (control characters → `?`, truncated at 80). The same pattern went into `UserMappingBulkImportService`'s `notifyAddress` copy and the CLI's `UserMappingValidator`. Also: `import-s3` now emits the "`--risk-usecase` is ignored because `--start-risk-assessment` is not set" warning `import` already had — silently ignoring it is how an operator ends up believing assessments ran. **Test skill.** `/aws-account-risk-assessment` (driver `scripts/test/test-e2e-aws-account-risk-assessment.sh`) gained three phases: the opt-in default (import a new account with no flag → mapping created, no assessment, no `AWS_ACCOUNT` asset; and the ignored-use-case warning), the deadline bound on both CLI and MCP, and a reworked idempotency phase that actually reaches the guard — it deletes the mapping so the account is new again while the assessment stays open, then asserts exit 0, a "skipped" line, no ❌, and still exactly one tracked assessment. Its **cleanup was also unsafe**: it deleted every risk assessment whose notes contained the substring `886` or `887`, which on a real environment means any assessment for a genuine AWS account whose id contains those digits. It now matches the owner-email prefix the service writes into the notes (`owner: e2e-awsra-`), which is both exact and stable across runs, sweeps mappings by that same prefix instead of this run's two timestamped ids (so earlier interrupted runs are cleaned up too), and finally removes the `AWS_ACCOUNT` basis assets — which nothing removed before, so every run leaked one. Accounts are now one per phase in a fixed `88[4-9]<stamp>000` shape, which is what the asset sweep matches. **Not verified in this session:** the environment had no Gradle distribution and no route to Maven Central, so the Kotlin changes are compile-unverified and neither the unit tests nor the E2E gates were run.

1	"""Optional secman backend integration (Phase 1 — no backend change needed).
     2	
     3	Flow: POST /api/auth/login (JWT arrives as `secman_auth` cookie, also usable
     4	as Bearer) -> PUT /api/assets/import per discovered asset (idempotent upsert,
     5	tags merged additively) -> POST /api/scan/upload-nmap for the raw nmap XML
     6	(creates Scan/ScanResult/ScanPort rows and links ports to assets in secman).
     7	
     8	Contract verified against src/backendng (AssetController.importAsset,

    25	IMPORT_ASSET_PATH = "/api/assets/import"

    41	class SecmanClient:
    42	    def __init__(self, config: SecmanConfig, timeout: float = 30.0):
    43	        self._config = config
    44	        self._client = httpx.Client(
    45	            base_url=config.base_url,
    46	            timeout=timeout,
    47	            headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT},
    48	        )
    49	        if config.token:

    55	
    56	    def close(self) -> None:

    58

    65	    # -- auth ----------------------------------------------------------------
    66	
    67	    def login(self) -> list[str]:
    68	        """Authenticate with username/password; returns the user's roles."""
    69	        if self._config.token:
    70	            return []  # token auth: roles unknown, validated on first request
    71	        try:
    72	            response = self._client.post(
    73	                LOGIN_PATH,
    74	                json={
    75	                    "username": self._config.username,
    76	                    "password": self._config.password,
    77	                },
    78	            )
    79	        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
    80	            raise SecmanError(f"cannot reach secman at {self._config.base_url}: {exc}") from exc
    81	        if response.status_code == 401:
    82	            raise SecmanError("secman login failed: invalid credentials")
    83	        if response.status_code != 200:
    84	            raise SecmanError(f"secman login failed: HTTP {response.status_code} {response.text[:200]}")
    85	        jwt = response.cookies.get("secman_auth")
    86	        if not jwt:
    87	            raise SecmanError("secman login succeeded but no secman_auth cookie was returned")
    88	        self._client.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {jwt}"
    89	        roles = response.json().get("roles", [])

    96	    def push_asset(self, host: DiscoveredHost, owner: str, enrichment: Enrichment | None = None) -> bool:
    97	        """Idempotent upsert of one asset. Returns True when newly created."""
    98	        description = f"Discovered by secman_intra_mon ({host.discovered_via or 'scan'})"

   103	            "type": "Network Host",
   104	            "owner": owner,
   105	            "ip": host.ip,
   106	            "networkZone": "INTERNAL",
   107	            "description": description,
   108	            "tags": self._asset_tags(host, enrichment),

   110	        response = self._request("PUT", IMPORT_ASSET_PATH, json=body)
   111	        payload = response.json()

   125	    def _request(self, method: str, path: str, **kwargs: Any) -> httpx.Response:
   126	        try:
   127	            response = self._client.request(method, path, **kwargs)
   128	        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
   129	            raise SecmanError(f"secman request {method} {path} failed: {exc}") from exc

   141	    @staticmethod

   146	        if host.mac_vendor:
   147	            tags["mac_vendor"] = host.mac_vendor
   148	        if host.os_guess:
   149	            tags["os_guess"] = host.os_guess
   150	        if host.open_ports:
   151	            tags["open_ports"] = ",".join(
   152	                f"{p.port}/{p.protocol}" for p in sorted(host.open_ports, key=lambda p: p.port)
   153	            )
   154	        if enrichment:
   155	            if enrichment.device_type:
   156	                tags["device_type"] = enrichment.device_type
   157	            if enrichment.criticality:
   158	                tags["criticality"] = enrichment.criticality

   162	def push_hosts(
   163	    client: SecmanClient,
   164	    hosts: list[DiscoveredHost],
   165	    owner: str,
   166	    xml_documents: list[str] | None = None,
   167	    enrichments: dict[str, Enrichment] | None = None,
   168	) -> PushSummary:
   169	    """Push all discovered assets, then upload nmap XML. Never raises on
   170	    individual asset failures — errors are collected into the summary."""
   171	    summary = PushSummary()
   172	    for host in hosts:
   173	        try:
   174	            if client.push_asset(host, owner, (enrichments or {}).get(host.ip)):
   175	                summary.assets_created += 1
   176	            else:
   177	                summary.assets_updated += 1
   178	        except (SecmanError, ValueError) as exc:
   179	            summary.errors.append(f"{host.ip}: {exc}")
   180	    for index, xml_text in enumerate(xml_documents or [], start=1):
   181	        try:
   182	            client.upload_nmap_xml(xml_text, f"intra-mon-scan-{index}.xml")
   183	            summary.xml_uploads += 1
   184	        except SecmanError as exc:
   185	            summary.errors.append(f"nmap xml upload {index}: {exc}")
   186	    return summary

     private fun matchesDeviceMetadata(asset: Asset, instance: String?, account: String?, domain: String?): Boolean {

             stored.trim().equals(incoming.trim(), ignoreCase = true)
         return compatible(asset.cloudInstanceId, instance) && compatible(asset.cloudAccountId, account) &&
             compatible(asset.adDomain, domain)
     }

    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if token:

    req = urllib.request.Request(
        os.environ["BASE_URL"] + path,
        data=json.dumps(data).encode() if data is not None else None,
        headers=headers, method=method,

    try:

    31	 * secman states the rule, the relay enforces it, and neither invents one.

   338	    @Post("/crowdstrike/servers/import")
   339	    open fun importServerVulnerabilities(
   340	        // The whole body is deserialized eagerly, and @ExecuteOn(BLOCKING) runs on virtual

  1570	    private fun queryAllMatchingDeviceIds(filter: String, token: AuthToken, pageLimit: Int = 100): List<String> {
  1571	        val ids = linkedSetOf<String>()
  1572	        var offset = 0
  1573	        while (true) {
  1574	            val uri = UriBuilder.of("/devices/queries/devices/v1")
  1575	                .queryParam("filter", filter).queryParam("limit", pageLimit).queryParam("offset", offset).build()
  1576	            val request = HttpRequest.GET<Any>(uri.toString())
  1577	                .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${token.accessToken}").header("Accept", "application/json")
  1578	            val response = try {
  1579	                httpClient.toBlocking().exchange(request, Map::class.java)
  1580	            } catch (e: HttpClientResponseException) {
  1581	                if (e.status.code == 404 && offset == 0) return emptyList()
  1582	                if (e.status.code == 429) throw RateLimitException("Rate limit during device lookup",
  1583	                    e.response.headers.get("Retry-After")?.toLongOrNull() ?: 30L, e)
  1584	                throw CrowdStrikeException("Falcon device lookup failed", e)
  1585	            }
  1586	            if (response.status.code != 200) throw CrowdStrikeException("Falcon device lookup failed")
  1587	            val body = response.body() as? Map<*, *> ?: throw CrowdStrikeException("Empty Falcon device lookup")
  1588	            if (!(body["errors"] as? List<*>).isNullOrEmpty()) throw CrowdStrikeException("Incomplete Falcon device lookup")
  1589	            val resources = body["resources"] as? List<*> ?: throw CrowdStrikeException("Missing Falcon device IDs")
  1590	            val page = resources.map { it?.toString() ?: throw CrowdStrikeException("Invalid Falcon device ID") }
  1591	            val pagination = (body["meta"] as? Map<*, *>)?.get("pagination") as? Map<*, *>
  1592	            val total = (pagination?.get("total") as? Number)?.toLong()
  1593	            if (page.any { !ids.add(it) }) throw CrowdStrikeException("Repeated Falcon device lookup page")
  1594	            offset += page.size
  1595	            if (total != null && offset.toLong() == total) return ids.toList()
  1596	            if (total != null && (offset > total || page.isEmpty())) throw CrowdStrikeException("Incomplete Falcon device enumeration")
  1597	            if (total == null && page.size < pageLimit) return ids.toList()
  1598	            if (offset >= 1000000) throw CrowdStrikeException("Falcon device enumeration exceeded safety limit")
  1599	        }
  1600	    }

448:Do not model cross-agent review gates as bridge child issues, freeform comments, ad-hoc `request_confirmation` cards, responder fields, mention grants, or broadened comment/interaction authorization. Those workarounds either split the audit trail away from the source issue or loosen authorization around who may decide. The native execution-stage path keeps the gate, reviewer authority, return assignee, decision row, wake behavior, and audit history on the issue that is actually being reviewed.
870:Use `request_confirmation` interactions for issue-scoped yes/no decisions that should render as cards in the issue thread. Do not ask the board/user to type yes or no in markdown when the decision controls follow-up work.
872:Use formal approvals for governed actions. Use `request_confirmation` for decisions such as:
883:  "kind": "request_confirmation",
912:- Create also accepts optional `addresseeAgentId` (an invokable same-company agent other than the creator) for structured agent-to-agent asks: Paperclip wakes the addressee with reason `interaction_pending`, only the addressee or a board user may resolve, and the pending card is omitted from the company attention feed. Not allowed with `request_confirmation.payload.toolAction` (`400`).

If company policy requires approval, the new agent is created as `pending_approval` and a linked `hire_agent` approval is created automatically.

**Do NOT** request hires unless you are a manager or CEO. IC agents should ask their manager.
Leave timer heartbeats off by default for new hires. Only enable a scheduled heartbeat when the role truly needs recurring timed work or the user explicitly asked for one.

Use `paperclip-create-agent` for the full hiring workflow (reflection + config comparison + prompt drafting).

### CEO strategy approval

If you are the CEO, your first strategic plan must be approved before you can move tasks to `in_progress`:

```
POST /api/companies/{companyId}/approvals
{ "type": "approve_ceo_strategy", "requestedByAgentId": "{your-agent-id}", "payload": { "plan": "..." } }
```

### Issue-thread confirmations

Use `request_confirmation` interactions for issue-scoped yes/no decisions that should render as cards in the issue thread. Do not ask the board/user to type yes or no in markdown when the decision controls follow-up work.

Use formal approvals for governed actions. Use `request_confirmation` for decisions such as:

- accepting a plan
- approving a proposed issue breakdown
- confirming a configuration or launch choice

Create a confirmation:

```json
POST /api/issues/{issueId}/interactions
{
  "kind": "request_confirmation",
  "idempotencyKey": "confirmation:{issueId}:{targetKey}:{targetVersion}",
  "title": "Plan approval",
  "continuationPolicy": "wake_assignee",
  "payload": {
    "version": 1,
    "prompt": "Accept this plan?",
    "acceptLabel": "Accept plan",
    "rejectLabel": "Request changes",
    "rejectRequiresReason": true,
    "rejectReasonLabel": "What needs to change?",
    "detailsMarkdown": "Review the latest plan document before accepting.",
    "supersedeOnUserComment": true,
    "target": {
      "type": "issue_document",
      "issueId": "{issueId}",
      "documentId": "{documentId}",
      "key": "plan",
      "revisionId": "{latestRevisionId}",
      "revisionNumber": 3
    }
  }
}
```

Resolver governance:

- **Omit `resolverPolicy` for a normal interaction.** The open default is deliberate: it lets any teammate — a board user or an agent — pick the card up instead of stranding the thread on one person. Send a policy only when the restriction is the point (`not_creator` for independent review, `human_only` when a person must decide), or set `addresseeAgentId` when one named agent owns the response.
- Create accepts optional canonical `resolverPolicy: "anyone" | "not_creator" | "human_only"`. Every interaction kind defaults to `anyone` when omitted. Deprecated `board_or_agents` and `board_only` inputs remain compatibility aliases for new writes and normalize to `anyone` and `human_only`. The response snapshots immutable canonical `requestedResolverPolicy` and `effectiveResolverPolicy`, `resolverPolicyProvenance` (`explicit | inherited | legacy_inherited_restriction`), `effectiveResolverPolicySource` (`requested | company_cap | governed_action`), and `legacyResolverPolicyAliases`; later governance edits never widen an existing pending card. `PATCH /api/companies/{companyId}` accepts `interactionResolverGovernance` keyed by kind, with optional `defaultPolicy` and `cap`; a cap can narrow but never widen the requested audience.
- Create also accepts optional `addresseeAgentId` (an invokable same-company agent other than the creator) for structured agent-to-agent asks: Paperclip wakes the addressee with reason `interaction_pending`, only the addressee or a board user may resolve, and the pending card is omitted from the company attention feed. Not allowed with `request_confirmation.payload.toolAction` (`400`).
- Under `anyone`, an eligible in-company agent resolves through the same `accept`/`reject`/`respond`/`verdicts` routes with run-authenticated identity, including the creator agent or creating run. `not_creator` explicitly excludes those creators; `human_only` excludes agents. Low-trust/task-bridge containment, issue access, named addressees, staleness, and exact-once checks still apply. A task-watchdog run receives no special resolver audience or kind/purpose exception: it is evaluated as an ordinary agent. `payload.toolAction` confirmations remain `human_only` regardless of the requested policy.
- Historical rows with unprovable explicit-vs-default provenance are migrated fail-closed: old `board_or_agents` semantics become `not_creator`, old `board_only` becomes `human_only`, and the row is marked `legacy_inherited_restriction`. Resolved outcomes and attribution are not rewritten.
- Resolution records a response only. Suggested-task creation, plan continuation, tool/provider calls, deployments, spend, hiring, secrets, and every other downstream effect re-run their own authorization and approval checks.

Rules:

- `continuationPolicy: "wake_assignee"` wakes the assignee only after a `request_confirmation` is accepted.
- Rejection does not wake the assignee by default. The board/user can add a normal comment when revisions are needed.
- Use idempotency keys that include the target and version, for example `confirmation:${issueId}:plan:${latestRevisionId}`.
- Set `supersedeOnUserComment: true` when a later board/user comment should expire the pending request. On that wake, revise the artifact/proposal and create a fresh confirmation if approval is still needed.
- A pending interaction is an explicit waiting path. Before ending the heartbeat, update the source issue into a visible waiting posture, normally `in_review`, and leave a comment that names the response needed and the effective audience.
- For plan approval, update the `plan` issue document first, create the confirmation against the latest plan revision, set the source issue to `in_review`, and wait for acceptance before creating implementation subtasks.

### Checkbox confirmations

Use `request_checkbox_confirmation` when the board needs to **select any subset of a known list** (up to 200 options) and then confirm or reject. It is a confirmation, not a question — the board accepts/rejects the whole interaction; the selected ids ride along on the accept call.

When to choose this kind over the others:

- Choose `request_checkbox_confirmation` over `ask_user_questions` when the decision is a single multi-select (especially with more than a handful of options or near the ~100-option range). `ask_user_questions` is for short structured forms, not long lists.
- Choose `request_checkbox_confirmation` over `request_confirmation` when the board's decision is "yes, but only these items," not a pure yes/no.
- Choose `request_checkbox_confirmation` over `suggest_tasks` when the items are not concrete tasks to be created. `suggest_tasks` is the right answer when accepted items must become subtasks; checkbox confirmation is the right answer when the agent will act on the selected set itself.

Create a checkbox confirmation:

```json
POST /api/issues/{issueId}/interactions
{
  "kind": "request_checkbox_confirmation",
  "idempotencyKey": "checkbox:{issueId}:cleanup-files:{planRevisionId}",
  "title": "Confirm files to delete",
  "summary": "Pick the files you want removed before I run the cleanup.",
  "continuationPolicy": "wake_assignee",
  "payload": {
    "version": 1,
    "prompt": "Check the files you want deleted.",
    "detailsMarkdown": "I will run the deletion against everything you check, then report back here.",
    "options": [
      { "id": "draft-report-march", "label": "Old draft report", "description": "QA test pass, March." },
      { "id": "tmp-export-2025", "label": "tmp/export-2025.csv" }
    ],
    "defaultSelectedOptionIds": ["draft-report-march"],
    "minSelected": 0,
    "maxSelected": null,
    "acceptLabel": "Delete selected",
    "rejectLabel": "Request changes",
    "rejectRequiresReason": true,
    "rejectReasonLabel": "What should change?",
    "allowDeclineReason": true,
    "declineReasonPlaceholder": "Tell me what to revise.",
    "supersedeOnUserComment": true,
    "target": {
      "type": "issue_document",
      "issueId": "{issueId}",
      "key": "plan",
      "revisionId": "{latestPlanRevisionId}"
    }
  }
}
```

Payload field reference (`RequestCheckboxConfirmationPayload`):

| Field                       | Type                                       | Default                          | Notes                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `version`                   | `1`                                        | required                         | Versioned for forward compatibility.                                                                                                        |
| `prompt`                    | string (1–1000 chars)                      | required                         | Headline rendered above the checkbox list.                                                                                                  |
| `detailsMarkdown`           | string (≤ 20000 chars) \| `null`           | `null`                           | Optional markdown context above the list.                                                                                                   |
| `options`                   | `[{ id, label, description? }]`            | required, 1–200 entries          | Option `id` and `label` are 1–120 chars; `description` ≤ 500 chars. Option ids must be unique within the payload.                            |
| `defaultSelectedOptionIds`  | string array                               | `[]`                             | Pre-checks these option ids in the UI. Each id must reference an option in `options`. Length must not exceed `maxSelected` when set.        |
| `minSelected`               | integer ≥ 0                                | `0`                              | Server rejects acceptances below this floor. Cannot exceed `options.length`.                                                                |
| `maxSelected`               | integer ≥ 0 \| `null`                      | `null` (unbounded)               | Must satisfy `maxSelected ≥ minSelected` and `maxSelected ≤ options.length` when set.                                                       |
| `acceptLabel`               | string (1–80) \| `null`                    | `null` (UI default)              | Button label for accept.                                                                                                                    |
| `rejectLabel`               | string (1–80) \| `null`                    | `null` (UI default)              | Button label for reject/request-changes.                                                                                                    |
| `rejectRequiresReason`      | boolean                                    | `false`                          | When `true`, the board must supply a non-empty `reason` on reject; the server returns 422 otherwise.                                         |
| `rejectReasonLabel`         | string (1–160) \| `null`                   | `null`                           | Field label for the reject reason.                                                                                                          |
| `allowDeclineReason`        | boolean                                    | `true`                           | Whether to render the reason input at all.                                                                                                  |
| `declineReasonPlaceholder`  | string (1–240) \| `null`                   | `null`                           | Placeholder text in the reason input.                                                                                                       |
| `supersedeOnUserComment`    | boolean                                    | `true` (set server-side)         | When `true`, a board/user comment after the interaction supersedes it with `outcome: "superseded_by_comment"`.                              |
| `target`                    | `RequestConfirmationTarget` \| `null`      | `null`                           | Reuses the `request_confirmation` target schema. Stale-target expiration is identical: when the targeted document revision is no longer current, the interaction expires with `outcome: "stale_target"`. |

Envelope defaults that differ from other kinds:

- `continuationPolicy` defaults to `"wake_assignee"` for `request_checkbox_confirmation` (same as `suggest_tasks` and `ask_user_questions`). Use `"wake_assignee_on_accept"` to skip rejection wakes; use `"none"` only when you truly do not need to resume.

Accept (board action, requires board/user role; agents creating the interaction cannot accept):

```json
POST /api/issues/{issueId}/interactions/{interactionId}/accept
{ "selectedOptionIds": ["draft-report-march", "tmp-export-2025"] }
```

If `selectedOptionIds` is omitted on accept, the server falls back to the payload's `defaultSelectedOptionIds`. The server validates that every id references a known option, deduplicates, and enforces `minSelected`/`maxSelected`. Unknown ids return 422.

Reject:

```json
POST /api/issues/{issueId}/interactions/{interactionId}/reject
{ "reason": "Keep the March draft; only delete tmp/export-2025.csv." }
```

`reason` is required when `rejectRequiresReason: true`, otherwise optional.

Resolved result (`RequestCheckboxConfirmationResult`):

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "outcome": "accepted",
  "selectedOptionIds": ["draft-report-march", "tmp-export-2025"]
}
```

Other outcomes match `request_confirmation`:

- `withdrawn` — `{ outcome: "withdrawn", reason }`. Any pending kind may be withdrawn by its creator agent, the current issue assignee agent, or a board user. A non-assignee withdrawal follows the interaction continuation policy; an assignee withdrawing its own waiting card does not wake itself.
- `issue_closed` — `{ outcome: "issue_closed" }`. Transitioning the issue to `done` or `cancelled` expires all pending interactions without continuation wakes; listing a terminal issue also performs a catch-up sweep for historical residue.

- `rejected` — `{ outcome: "rejected", reason, commentId }`. `selectedOptionIds` is absent.
- `superseded_by_comment` — `{ outcome: "superseded_by_comment", commentId }`. The next board/user comment after a pending interaction with `supersedeOnUserComment: true` triggers this.
- `stale_target` — `{ outcome: "stale_target", staleTarget }`. Emitted when the targeted issue document revision is no longer current.

- Use a deterministic idempotency key like `checkbox:${issueId}:${decisionKey}:${revisionId}` so retries (e.g. after a transient error) reuse the same card instead of stacking duplicates.
- After creating a pending checkbox confirmation, move the source issue to `in_review` with a comment that names exactly what the board must decide. Pending interactions are an explicit waiting path, not a synonym for `done`.

Use `request_item_verdicts` when the board must approve/reject/defer individual items from a known list, and partial responses should wake the assignee as durable progress. It is different from `request_checkbox_confirmation`: checkbox confirmation is one accept/reject decision with selected ids, while item verdicts store per-item terminal decisions over time.

- A pending interaction is an explicit waiting path. Before ending the heartbeat, update the source issue into a visible waiting posture, normally `in_review`, and leave a comment that names the response needed and the effective audience.
- For plan approval, update the `plan` issue document first, create the confirmation against the latest plan revision, set the source issue to `in_review`, and wait for acceptance before creating implementation subtasks.

### Checkbox confirmations

Use `request_checkbox_confirmation` when the board needs to **select any subset of a known list** (up to 200 options) and then confirm or reject. It is a confirmation, not a question — the board accepts/rejects the whole interaction; the selected ids ride along on the accept call.

When to choose this kind over the others:

- Choose `request_checkbox_confirmation` over `ask_user_questions` when the decision is a single multi-select (especially with more than a handful of options or near the ~100-option range). `ask_user_questions` is for short structured forms, not long lists.
- Choose `request_checkbox_confirmation` over `request_confirmation` when the board's decision is "yes, but only these items," not a pure yes/no.
- Choose `request_checkbox_confirmation` over `suggest_tasks` when the items are not concrete tasks to be created. `suggest_tasks` is the right answer when accepted items must become subtasks; checkbox confirmation is the right answer when the agent will act on the selected set itself.

Create a checkbox confirmation:

```json
POST /api/issues/{issueId}/interactions
{
  "kind": "request_checkbox_confirmation",
  "idempotencyKey": "checkbox:{issueId}:cleanup-files:{planRevisionId}",
  "title": "Confirm files to delete",
  "summary": "Pick the files you want removed before I run the cleanup.",
  "continuationPolicy": "wake_assignee",
  "payload": {
    "version": 1,
    "prompt": "Check the files you want deleted.",
    "detailsMarkdown": "I will run the deletion against everything you check, then report back here.",
    "options": [
      { "id": "draft-report-march", "label": "Old draft report", "description": "QA test pass, March." },
      { "id": "tmp-export-2025", "label": "tmp/export-2025.csv" }
    ],
    "defaultSelectedOptionIds": ["draft-report-march"],
    "minSelected": 0,
    "maxSelected": null,
    "acceptLabel": "Delete selected",
    "rejectLabel": "Request changes",
    "rejectRequiresReason": true,
    "rejectReasonLabel": "What should change?",
    "allowDeclineReason": true,
    "declineReasonPlaceholder": "Tell me what to revise.",
    "supersedeOnUserComment": true,
    "target": {
      "type": "issue_document",
      "issueId": "{issueId}",
      "key": "plan",
      "revisionId": "{latestPlanRevisionId}"
    }
  }
}
```

Payload field reference (`RequestCheckboxConfirmationPayload`):

| Field                       | Type                                       | Default                          | Notes                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `version`                   | `1`                                        | required                         | Versioned for forward compatibility.                                                                                                        |
| `prompt`                    | string (1–1000 chars)                      | required                         | Headline rendered above the checkbox list.                                                                                                  |
| `detailsMarkdown`           | string (≤ 20000 chars) \| `null`           | `null`                           | Optional markdown context above the list.                                                                                                   |
| `options`                   | `[{ id, label, description? }]`            | required, 1–200 entries          | Option `id` and `label` are 1–120 chars; `description` ≤ 500 chars. Option ids must be unique within the payload.                            |
| `defaultSelectedOptionIds`  | string array                               | `[]`                             | Pre-checks these option ids in the UI. Each id must reference an option in `options`. Length must not exceed `maxSelected` when set.        |
| `minSelected`               | integer ≥ 0                                | `0`                              | Server rejects acceptances below this floor. Cannot exceed `options.length`.                                                                |
| `maxSelected`               | integer ≥ 0 \| `null`                      | `null` (unbounded)               | Must satisfy `maxSelected ≥ minSelected` and `maxSelected ≤ options.length` when set.                                                       |
| `acceptLabel`               | string (1–80) \| `null`                    | `null` (UI default)              | Button label for accept.                                                                                                                    |
| `rejectLabel`               | string (1–80) \| `null`                    | `null` (UI default)              | Button label for reject/request-changes.                                                                                                    |
| `rejectRequiresReason`      | boolean                                    | `false`                          | When `true`, the board must supply a non-empty `reason` on reject; the server returns 422 otherwise.                                         |
| `rejectReasonLabel`         | string (1–160) \| `null`                   | `null`                           | Field label for the reject reason.                                                                                                          |
| `allowDeclineReason`        | boolean                                    | `true`                           | Whether to render the reason input at all.                                                                                                  |
| `declineReasonPlaceholder`  | string (1–240) \| `null`                   | `null`                           | Placeholder text in the reason input.                                                                                                       |
| `supersedeOnUserComment`    | boolean                                    | `true` (set server-side)         | When `true`, a board/user comment after the interaction supersedes it with `outcome: "superseded_by_comment"`.                              |
| `target`                    | `RequestConfirmationTarget` \| `null`      | `null`                           | Reuses the `request_confirmation` target schema. Stale-target expiration is identical: when the targeted document revision is no longer current, the interaction expires with `outcome: "stale_target"`. |

Envelope defaults that differ from other kinds:

- `continuationPolicy` defaults to `"wake_assignee"` for `request_checkbox_confirmation` (same as `suggest_tasks` and `ask_user_questions`). Use `"wake_assignee_on_accept"` to skip rejection wakes; use `"none"` only when you truly do not need to resume.

Accept (board action, requires board/user role; agents creating the interaction cannot accept):

```json
POST /api/issues/{issueId}/interactions/{interactionId}/accept
{ "selectedOptionIds": ["draft-report-march", "tmp-export-2025"] }
```

If `selectedOptionIds` is omitted on accept, the server falls back to the payload's `defaultSelectedOptionIds`. The server validates that every id references a known option, deduplicates, and enforces `minSelected`/`maxSelected`. Unknown ids return 422.

Reject:

```json
POST /api/issues/{issueId}/interactions/{interactionId}/reject
{ "reason": "Keep the March draft; only delete tmp/export-2025.csv." }
```

`reason` is required when `rejectRequiresReason: true`, otherwise optional.

Resolved result (`RequestCheckboxConfirmationResult`):

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "outcome": "accepted",
  "selectedOptionIds": ["draft-report-march", "tmp-export-2025"]
}
```

Other outcomes match `request_confirmation`:

- `withdrawn` — `{ outcome: "withdrawn", reason }`. Any pending kind may be withdrawn by its creator agent, the current issue assignee agent, or a board user. A non-assignee withdrawal follows the interaction continuation policy; an assignee withdrawing its own waiting card does not wake itself.
- `issue_closed` — `{ outcome: "issue_closed" }`. Transitioning the issue to `done` or `cancelled` expires all pending interactions without continuation wakes; listing a terminal issue also performs a catch-up sweep for historical residue.

- `rejected` — `{ outcome: "rejected", reason, commentId }`. `selectedOptionIds` is absent.
- `superseded_by_comment` — `{ outcome: "superseded_by_comment", commentId }`. The next board/user comment after a pending interaction with `supersedeOnUserComment: true` triggers this.
- `stale_target` — `{ outcome: "stale_target", staleTarget }`. Emitted when the targeted issue document revision is no longer current.

Best practice:

- Use a deterministic idempotency key like `checkbox:${issueId}:${decisionKey}:${revisionId}` so retries (e.g. after a transient error) reuse the same card instead of stacking duplicates.
- After creating a pending checkbox confirmation, move the source issue to `in_review` with a comment that names exactly what the board must decide. Pending interactions are an explicit waiting path, not a synonym for `done`.
- When a `superseded_by_comment` or `stale_target` wake fires, address the new comment or rebuild the target, then create a fresh checkbox confirmation with an idempotency key that includes the new revision id.

### Item verdict requests

Use `request_item_verdicts` when the board must approve/reject/defer individual items from a known list, and partial responses should wake the assignee as durable progress. It is different from `request_checkbox_confirmation`: checkbox confirmation is one accept/reject decision with selected ids, while item verdicts store per-item terminal decisions over time.

     9	# SecMan static finalizer
    10	
    11	## When to use
    12	
    13	Use for a static/offline documentation-to-code alignment task in `/Users/flake/sources/misc/secman`, especially when the assignment requires `dev`, mechanically proven documentation edits, a Paperclip trailer, no push, and explicit unavailable-gate reporting.
    14	
    15	Do not use for product behavior changes, service startup, full builds, E2E, credential-backed checks, or resolving an ambiguous backend/client contract without an owner decision.
    16	
    17	## Inputs / context to gather
    18	
    19	1. Read the assigned Paperclip issue, required trailer, intended status/blocker owner, and side-effect limits.
    20	2. Confirm the root branch is `dev`; inspect root plus every relevant independent extension checkout with `git status --short` before edits.
    21	3. Read the claimed documentation sections and the authoritative source/call sites. For Web Check v1, compare `extensions/secman_web_check/src/secman.py` with backend `IntegrationDtos.kt`.
    22	
    23	## Procedure
    24	
    25	1. Treat pre-existing root or extension dirt, merge conflicts, untracked files, and dependency-file changes as user-owned. Do not reset, stash, repair, stage, or include them.
    26	2. Make only documentation changes directly supported by the current source. Never change application behavior merely to make documentation true.
    27	3. Run static in-scope checks: `./scripts/owasp-check.sh`, `./scripts/check-skill-sync.sh` (or `--verbose` when assigned), and `git diff --check`. Run focused suites only when their checkout is clean and the task permits it.
    28	4. If documentation drift is proven, stage only the named paths and commit on `dev` with `Co-Authored-By: Paperclip <noreply@paperclip.ing>`. Do not push.
    29	5. For the `bodyLength` mismatch—Web Check emits `inventory.exposure.bodyLength` while backend `WebExposureInput` does not accept/persist it—stop. The product/integration owner must choose add-to-v1 or remove-from-client; only then align implementation, canonical fixture, and tests in clean checkouts.
    30	6. Make at most one intended Paperclip disposition. Capture the result and GET/read back issue/comment/blocker state. If `blocked` rejects an absent or board-owned `unblockDescriptor`, do not retry the same mutation; use an eligible owner, a real human decision interaction, or a first-class blocker.
    31	7. Report available static results separately from unavailable aggregate/runtime/build/E2E gates.
    32	
    33	## Efficiency plan
    34	
    35	- Preflight branch and all worktree status before source browsing or test execution; this prevents touching user-owned extensions.
    36	- Start from the claimed doc line and its authoritative source instead of broad rewrites.
    37	- Stop aggregate validation immediately when `extensions/secman_visual_check/tests/fixtures/integration-run-v1.json` is absent; retain separately passing focused checks without calling the aggregate gate successful.
    38	
    39	## Pitfalls and fixes
    40	
    41	- `check-integration-contract.sh --run` exits before tests because `integration-run-v1.json` is absent -> report aggregate validation unavailable, not failed product behavior.
    42	- Web Check pytest cannot collect because of existing merge conflicts, such as `src/models.py:178` -> preserve the checkout and report its suite unchecked.
    43	- `bodyLength` exists on one side of the contract only -> do not silently add persistence or drop the client field; require an owner decision.
    44	- Paperclip `blocked` mutation rejected -> preserve successful evidence/comment writes, stop mutation loops, and report the verified remaining state.
    45

    47	
    48	- `dev` was verified before editing and committing.
    49	- Dirty root/extension state is unchanged; commit, if any, is path-scoped and unpushed.

    52	- Missing/unchecked gates are explicitly separated from passes.
    53	- Contract conflicts include the owner decision needed to resume.
    54	- Paperclip outcome has returned-result plus read-back evidence.

     9	# SecMan static finalizer
    10	
    11	## When to use
    12	
    13	Use for a static/offline documentation-to-code alignment task in `/Users/flake/sources/misc/secman`, especially when the assignment requires `dev`, mechanically proven documentation edits, a Paperclip trailer, no push, and explicit unavailable-gate reporting.
    14	
    15	Do not use for product behavior changes, service startup, full builds, E2E, credential-backed checks, or resolving an ambiguous backend/client contract without an owner decision.
    16	
    17	## Inputs / context to gather
    18	
    19	1. Read the assigned Paperclip issue, required trailer, intended status/blocker owner, and side-effect limits.
    20	2. Confirm the root branch is `dev`; inspect root plus every relevant independent extension checkout with `git status --short` before edits.
    21	3. Read the claimed documentation sections and the authoritative source/call sites. For Web Check v1, compare `extensions/secman_web_check/src/secman.py` with backend `IntegrationDtos.kt`.
    22	
    23	## Procedure
    24	
    25	1. Treat pre-existing root or extension dirt, merge conflicts, untracked files, and dependency-file changes as user-owned. Do not reset, stash, repair, stage, or include them.
    26	2. Make only documentation changes directly supported by the current source. Never change application behavior merely to make documentation true.
    27	3. Run static in-scope checks: `./scripts/owasp-check.sh`, `./scripts/check-skill-sync.sh` (or `--verbose` when assigned), and `git diff --check`. Run focused suites only when their checkout is clean and the task permits it.
    28	4. If documentation drift is proven, stage only the named paths and commit on `dev` with `Co-Authored-By: Paperclip <noreply@paperclip.ing>`. Do not push.
    29	5. For the `bodyLength` mismatch—Web Check emits `inventory.exposure.bodyLength` while backend `WebExposureInput` does not accept/persist it—stop. The product/integration owner must choose add-to-v1 or remove-from-client; only then align implementation, canonical fixture, and tests in clean checkouts.
    30	6. Make at most one intended Paperclip disposition. Capture the result and GET/read back issue/comment/blocker state. If `blocked` rejects an absent or board-owned `unblockDescriptor`, do not retry the same mutation; use an eligible owner, a real human decision interaction, or a first-class blocker.
    31	7. Report available static results separately from unavailable aggregate/runtime/build/E2E gates.
    32	
    33	## Efficiency plan
    34	
    35	- Preflight branch and all worktree status before source browsing or test execution; this prevents touching user-owned extensions.
    36	- Start from the claimed doc line and its authoritative source instead of broad rewrites.
    37	- Stop aggregate validation immediately when `extensions/secman_visual_check/tests/fixtures/integration-run-v1.json` is absent; retain separately passing focused checks without calling the aggregate gate successful.
    38	
    39	## Pitfalls and fixes
    40	
    41	- `check-integration-contract.sh --run` exits before tests because `integration-run-v1.json` is absent -> report aggregate validation unavailable, not failed product behavior.
    42	- Web Check pytest cannot collect because of existing merge conflicts, such as `src/models.py:178` -> preserve the checkout and report its suite unchecked.
    43	- `bodyLength` exists on one side of the contract only -> do not silently add persistence or drop the client field; require an owner decision.
    44	- Paperclip `blocked` mutation rejected -> preserve successful evidence/comment writes, stop mutation loops, and report the verified remaining state.
    45

    47	
    48	- `dev` was verified before editing and committing.
    49	- Dirty root/extension state is unchanged; commit, if any, is path-scoped and unpushed.
    50	- Documentation claims match inspected authoritative source.

    52	- Missing/unchecked gates are explicitly separated from passes.
    53	- Contract conflicts include the owner decision needed to resume.
    54	- Paperclip outcome has returned-result plus read-back evidence.
